You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Defer Sign-In After Adoption [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +12.0%, measured +3.1% (p=0.081036), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Photo Upload Customization Guidance [adoption, copy]: predicted +9.0%, measured -0.5% (p=0.857471), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Add Interactive Tips to Waiting Screen [home, wait_info]: predicted +6.0%, measured +5.0% (p=0.010744), won
- round 1: Grid Layout for Path Options [choose_path, layout]: predicted +4.0%, measured -1.4% (p=0.317699), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Pet Preview Screen Before Adoption Certificate [adoption, new_screen]: predicted +3.0%, measured +15.4% (p=0.0), won
- round 2: Interactive Controls Tutorial on Home Intro [finish, redesign]: predicted +2.0%, measured -3.0% (p=0.368743), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Pet Command Carousel on Waiting Screen [home, wait_info]: predicted +4.0%, measured +5.7% (p=0.000151), won
- round 2: Account Sync Warning Copy on Sign In [sign_in, copy]: predicted +1.0%, measured +0.4% (p=0.82048), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Time Estimate and Progress Counter on Choose Path [choose_path, hint]: predicted +1.0%, measured -2.2% (p=0.120914), lost: no clear effect

Previous lessons:
Adding interactive tips to the waiting screen (wait_info) was helpful and yielded a statistically significant gain (+5.0%).
Deferring sign-in (reorder), photo upload copy guidance (copy), and grid layout changes (layout) showed no clear effect.
Effect predictions were consistently too high across all tests, overestimating both positive gains and non-significant changes.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Waiting screen enhancements (wait_info) are helpful and consistently yield statistically significant gains.
Adding a pet preview screen before the adoption certificate (new_screen) is helpful and produced a large significant gain (+15.4%).
Copy adjustments (copy), layout changes (layout), sign-in reordering (reorder), tutorials (redesign), and progress hints (hint) showed no clear effect.
Predictions underestimated large wins, such as the pet preview screen (+3.0% predicted vs +15.4% measured).
Predictions were generally too high for changes that showed no clear effect.
